extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners evaluating creative writing, computational creativity, and LLM-generated texts
extracted.subtask_description: A protocol (Torrance Tests for Creative Writing, TTCW) for artifact-centric binary evaluation of creativity in short fictional stories, with 14 yes/no tests across Fluency, Flexibility, Originality, and Elaboration, each accompanied by a short free-text rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative Pacing (TTCW Fluency1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the manipulation of time in terms of compression or stretching feel appropriate and balanced?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refers to control of perceived speed/rhythm of the story (compression vs. stretching of story time vs. real-world time). Assess whether manipulation of time is used for dramatic effect and whether it improves reader engagement. Experts suggested looking for balanced compression/stretching; include a 1–3 sentence rationale. Binary (Yes/No).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scene vs Exposition (TTCW Fluency2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the story display awareness and insight into the balance between scene and summary/exposition?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines 'Scene' as dramatized, real-time moments (dialogue, action) and 'Exposition' as summary or background. Evaluate whether the story balances scene and summary appropriately for pace and engagement (e.g., enough dialogue to compensate for backstory). Provide brief rationale. Binary (Yes/No).

rubrics_metrics.name: Language Proficiency & Literary Devices (TTCW Fluency3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the story make sophisticated use of idiom or metaphor or literary allusion?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess presence and sophistication of figurative language, metaphors, idioms, and literary allusion — whether they add depth, are surprising/skillful, or feel forced. Expert examples and LLM prompt templates exist (list metaphors/allusions and judge success). Provide 1–3 sentence rationale. Binary (Yes/No).

rubrics_metrics.name: Narrative Ending (TTCW Fluency4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the end of the story feel natural and earned, as opposed to arbitrary or abrupt?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the ending arises from the story's build-up (not a rushed or 'author tired' ending). A strong ending provides closure and ties central conflicts/questions; a hasty ending feels disjointed. Use a short explanatory rationale. Binary (Yes/No).

rubrics_metrics.name: Understandability & Coherence (TTCW Fluency5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do the different elements of the story work together to form a unified, engaging, and satisfying whole?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess narrative coherence: whether beginning leads through middle to end deliberately, and whether scenes/characters/dialogue serve the story. Look for logical flow and unity vs disorder. Provide brief rationale. Binary (Yes/No).

rubrics_metrics.name: Perspective & Voice Flexibility (TTCW Flexibility1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the story provide diverse perspectives, and if there are unlikeable characters, are their perspectives presented convincingly and accurately?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the author's ability to inhabit multiple voices/perspectives (including morally ambiguous or unlikeable characters) convincingly. Consider omniscient vs limited narration and authenticity of viewpoints. Provide 1–3 sentence justification. Binary (Yes/No).

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional Flexibility (TTCW Flexibility2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the story achieve a good balance between interiority and exteriority, in a way that feels emotionally flexible?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance action/dialogue/observable behavior (exteriority) with inner life/thoughts/feelings (interiority). Evaluate whether emotional portrayal avoids being shallow or overly introspective and supports emotional realism. Provide brief rationale. Binary (Yes/No).

rubrics_metrics.name: Structural Flexibility (TTCW Flexibility3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the story contain turns that are both surprising and appropriate?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether plot twists, revelations, or turns surprise the reader yet remain believable and consistent within the story's rules and character motivations. Avoid shocks that break established constraints. Explain each surprising element and judge appropriateness; provide short rationale. Binary (Yes/No).

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality in Theme and Content (TTCW Originality1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Will an average reader of this story obtain a unique and original idea from reading it?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the story offers new insights, perspectives, or thematic contributions (not just plot novelty). Consider whether the piece provokes new understanding or purpose for being in the world. Provide brief reasoning and Yes/No. Binary (Yes/No).

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality in Thought (TTCW Originality2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the story an original piece of writing without any cliches?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge presence of clichés, recycled tropes, or stereotyped one-dimensional characters; determine whether such elements detract from originality. Experts emphasize avoidance of predictable, overused ideas. List clichés if present and explain impact; provide Yes/No. Binary (Yes/No).

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality in Form & Structure (TTCW Originality3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the story show originality in its form?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess innovative use of narrative form/structure, format, genre hybridity, non-linear timelines, unusual narrative voices or typographic/format experiments. Determine whether formal choices provide a fresh experience or deeper thematic exploration. List devices used and judge success; provide short rationale. Binary (Yes/No).

rubrics_metrics.name: World Building & Setting (TTCW Elaboration1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the writer make the fictional world believable at the sensory level?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate use of sensory detail and self-consistent world-building that grounds the story (even in SF/fantasy). Consider setting informing action and atmosphere without falling into pathetic fallacy. Judges should note sensory details and consistency and provide brief rationale. Binary (Yes/No).

rubrics_metrics.name: Character Development (TTCW Elaboration2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does each character in the story feel developed at the appropriate complexity level, ensuring that no character feels like they are present simply to satisfy a plot requirement?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish flat (one-dimensional) vs complex (round) characters; assess whether characters evolve, have motivations, and are multi-faceted. List characters and level of development; explain whether they feel necessary and credible. Provide short rationale. Binary (Yes/No).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rhetorical Complexity / Subtext (TTCW Elaboration3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are there passages in the story that involve subtext and when there is subtext, does it enrich the story’s setting or does it feel forced?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate surface-level actions/dialogue vs underlying meanings (subtext). Determine whether subtext adds layers, complexity, or resonates with themes, or whether it feels contrived. Provide examples of subtextual passages and judge their enrichment; include brief rationale. Binary (Yes/No).
